texts.value: Involved in the breakdown of putrescine. Catalyzes the ATP-dependent gamma-glutamylation of putrescine, producing gamma-L-glutamylputrescine. Absolutely essential to utilize putrescine as both nitrogen and carbon sources and to decrease the toxicity of putrescine, which can lead to inhibition of cell growth and protein synthesis. In vitro is also able to use several diamines, and spermidine and spermine, instead of putrescine, but with a much lower activity, and cannot catalyze the gamma-glutamylation of ornithine or GABA (PubMed:18495664)

Dehydrogenase involved in the degradation of putrescine (PubMed:15590624, PubMed:22636776). Acts as a non-specific aldehyde dehydrogenase that can catalyze three separate reactions in putrescine catabolism: the oxidation of gamma-glutamyl-gamma-aminobutyraldehyde to gamma-glutamyl-gamma-aminobutyrate (gamma-Glu-GABA), the oxidation 4-aminobutanal (gamma-aminobutyraldehyde) to 4-aminobutanoate (gamma-aminobutyrate or GABA) and the oxidation of succinate semialdehyde to succinate (PubMed:15590624, PubMed:22636776). In vitro, it exhibits broad substrate specificity for various aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes (PubMed:18668238). It can use both NAD(+) and NADP(+), but NAD(+) is significantly preferred over NADP(+) for many aldehydes (PubMed:18668238). Among the aldehydes tested, 3-hydroxypropanal (3-hydroxypropionaldehyde or 3-HPA) is the best substrate, followed by 3-methylbutanal (isovaleraldehyde), propanal (propionaldehyde), butanal (butyraldehyde), pentanal (valeraldehyde), benzaldehyde, furfural (2-furaldehyde) and acetaldehyde (PubMed:18668238). The enzyme cannot use formaldehyde (PubMed:18668238). It might play a role in propionate and/or acetic acid metabolisms in addition to its function in putrescine metabolism (PubMed:18668238)

Activity is enhanced in the presence of disulfide reductants such as dithiothreitol (DTT) or 2-mercaptoethanol (PubMed:18668238). Activity is completely inhibited in the presence of heavy metals (mercury, silver) or sodium hydrogensulfite, and strongly inhibited in the presence of lithium, copper and zinc ions (PubMed:18668238). Slightly inhibited by potassium, sodium and ammonium ions (PubMed:18668238)
